name: Ogre (Far Distant Future Publishing)
body:
Ogres have earned a reputation for being big, ugly, crude, and cruel. While they are actually somewhat more complex than people usually give them credit for, that doesn’t change the fact that an encounter with an ogre is a terrifying experience, and one that few people walk away from unharmed.

Physical

Ogres stand about twice the height of humans, averaging 10 feet for males and only slightly shorter for females. They are related to giants, but like trolls they are much more varied in their appearance than true giants. Mutations and deformities are common among ogres, which most people attribute to inbreeding—and while incest is indeed common among ogres, this is only part of a complex story.

Ogres are extremely sensitive to their environment—physical, social, emotional, and magical. It has been noted that ogre children who live near humans look more human, while those who live near goblins look more goblinoid, and so on. More than that, though, ogre behavior tends to reflect and amplify the worst aspects of their neighbors. The ogres who live near warlike peoples will be bloodthirsty cannibals.

Those who live near slavers will capture and torture their enemies. Those who live near magic-abusing tyrants will worship demons and have beastly mutations.

Among all giant species, ogres are particularly fecund. It is rumored that they can reproduce by extraordinary methods in areas fueled by particularly strong negative emptions—for example, ogres developing vestigial twins that fall off and grow into new ogres, or ogres spontaneously being born to orcs or hill giants. While these cases are hard to verify, they lend further credence to the rumors that ogres are not a completely naturally-occurring species.

Social

Ogres have no social filters, taboos, or restraints. They act almost completely on impulse, indulging their every whim and desire. While this may be interpreted as a sign of stupidity, ogres are actually quite cunning. Rather, they seem to have difficulty developing empathy—what some have described as a state of “perpetual emotional infancy.”

While different individuals favor different vices, the driving principal of ogre society as a whole is cruelty. Ogres are almost drawn to acts of savagery and mercilessness by instinct. Whatever forces conspired to create these creatures did so as a mockery of other humanoids, making them ugly and mean-tempered, finding humor in the suffering of others. They are not completely irredeemable, but exceptions are few and far between. Even offspring of mixed-ogre ancestry have difficulty controlling their urge to wantonly murder and destroy.

The one saving grace of ogre society is their love for their own kin. While ogres do quarrel amongst themselves, they don’t display the level of nastiness and brutality that they show to other peoples. Contrary to their usual behavior, they care for their children and share resources among their tribe. Ogres raised among giants, orcs, or even humans, may learn to adopt some members of other species as their own family, and may have an easier time socializing in general.

Alignment And Religion

The typical ogre is Chaotic Evil, only ever about their own agenda and wishing nothing by harm upon everyone else. While some ogres can fight these instincts and learn to channel their urges into more constructive behaviors, this is a very difficult task. Few ogres are able to stray from both Chaotic and Evil—with most keeping at least one of these elements in their alignment.

Demon-worship comes naturally to ogres, at least for those who choose to worship at all.

Many demons make enticing offers to ogre tribes, catering to their worst indulgences to garner favor.

Names

Ogres speak a dialect of giant considered crude by most other speakers of that tongue. Their names are usually very short, featuring harsh, guttural sounds that don’t resemble typical giant names. Many ogres who learn Common—even if only a few words—pride themselves in adopting a nickname in that language as well.

Some typical ogre names include the following (choose or roll 1d12): 1 Aggack, 2 Bungo, 3 Bwerp, 4 Glub, 5 Gully, 6 Krupp, 7 Pflogg, 8 Shmork, 9 Skrugga, 10 Uggugg, 11 Vixxo, 12 Yelk

Meanwhile, typical ogre nicknames in Common include (choose or roll 1d12): 1 Chop, 2 Crash, 3 Crunch, 4 Crush, 5 Fist, 6 Hulk, 7 Mush, 8 Rip, 9 Shred, 10 Shrug, 11 Smash, 12 Tug

Note: While the ogre as presented here is equivalent to example presented in the Pathfinder Roleplaying Game Advanced Race Guide, its RP cost is lower because the ability score modifier cost is calculated differently—and, in our estimation, more equitably and accurately.

Standard Species Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You are strong are hearty but somewhat dim-witted and dull, and you have difficulty controlling your hateful urges. Your ability score modifiers are +4 Str, +2 Con, –2 Int, –2 Cha [flexible, advanced Str, penalty ×2]. (4) Note: After your modifiers for being size Large are incorporated, your net ability score modifiers are: +6 Str, +2 Con, –2 Dex, –2 Int, –2 Cha.
Size As a Large creature, you have a –1 size penalty on attack rolls, a –1 size penalty to your Armor Class, a +1 size bonus to your CMB, and a –4 size penalty on Stealth checks. As a Large creature, you occupy a space of 10 feet by 10 feet. Your reach is 10 feet. You take a further –2 penalty to Dex, and gain a further +2 bonus to Str. (7)
Type You are a Humanoid with the giant subtype. (0)
Speed Your base speed is 30 feet. (0)
Languages You begin play speaking Giant. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any of the following languages: Common, Draconic, Goblin, or Orc. (0)
Alternate Species Traits
Darkvision You have darkvision 60 feet. (2)
Low-light Vision You can see twice as far as a human in starlight, moonlight, torchlight, and similar conditions of poor illumination. You retain the ability to distinguish color and detail under these conditions. (1)
Natural Armor Your tough, resilient skin provides a +2 natural armor bonus to AC. (3)
Reach You have a reach of 10 feet. (1)
Total: 18 RP (advanced)
Alternate Species Traits
Fast You move in a fluid, crouching motion, staying low to the ground, sometimes even moving on all fours like an animal. Your base speed is 40 feet, but your natural armor bonus is reduced by 1. This trait alters speed and natural armor.
Gore Your head is misshapen and malformed, featuring a thick skull with one or more protruding horns or a jutting jaw with large tusks. You gain a gore attack; this is a primary natural attack that deals 1d8 damage. You take a further –2 penalty to both Intelligence and Charisma, which stacks with your other ability score modifiers. This trait alters ability score modifiers.
Pickin You are thinner than most of your kin, and have hands that end in sharp claws, giving you two claw attacks. These are primary natural attacks that deal 1d6 damage each. You blend into your forest surroundings thank to your spiky, bark-like skin, giving you a +4 species bonus on Stealth checks while in forest terrain. You do not gain the ogre’s usual +2 bonus to Con. This trait alters ability score modifiers.
Scent Your eyes are underdeveloped, but your sense of smell is greatly heightened. You gain the scent B1 universal monster ability. This trait replaces darkvision and low-light vision.
Shaggra You are covered in fur, with an apelike appearance, including stunted legs and massive arms. Your base speed is reduced by 10 feet, but your speed is never reduced by armor or encumbrance. You gain two slam attacks; these are primary natural attacks that deal 1d6 damage. This trait alters speed.
Thickin Your ridiculously oversized head is filled with razor-sharp teeth, giving you a bite attack. This is a primary natural attack that deals 1d6 damage. You take a –2 penalty to Dex, which stacks with your other ability score modifiers. This trait alters ability score modifiers.
Alternative Favored Class Bonuses
Barbarian Add +1 to your total number of rage rounds per day.
Brawler Add +1 to your CMD when resisting a grapple or sunder attempt.
Fighter Choose one weapon or natural attack that you are proficient with. Add +1/2 on critical hit confirmation rolls made while using that weapon (maximum bonus of +4). This bonus does not stack with Critical Focus.
Rogue Add a +1 bonus on your sneak attack damage rolls against any target suffering from a fear effect.
Slayer Gain +1/6 of a new slayer talent.
Sorcerer Add +1 to the total number of rounds per day you can use the claws abyssal bloodline power. You must possess the applicable power to select this bonus.
Warpriest Add +1/4 to your effective warpriest level when determining the damage of your sacred weapon.

Awesome Ancestries: Species of Horror Vol. 2. © 2025, Far Distant Future Publishing; Author: Bryan Mangum.
